doc.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06

title: New Orleans' indifference to music as a profession
summary: Huntington says the city treats music as not a real job, even for a middle-aged player today.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: All right, Bill, you were, I think, discussing the nonchalance of New Orleans towards this music. Maybe you want to pick that thread up again and amplify a little bit about it.

Well, I always felt, as you said, there was a certain indifference to music here as a profession. I mean, even to this day, people will look at somebody like me. I'm a middle-aged, older, middle-aged man, and people will look at me and say, you know, it's not like I'm a professional. It's like I play with a band, but what is your real job? You know, I mean,
I haven't heard that in a while, but I'm sure.
